nodes.name: NiFe-LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.9 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.6 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 1.4 mmol CTAB were dissolved in a mixture of 36 mL MeOH and 6 mL water and stirred to form a clear solution. Nickel foam (about 4×3 cm) was carefully cleaned with the concentrated HCl solution (37 wt.%) in an ultrasound bath for 5 min to remove the surface NiO layer, and then water and MeOH were used for 5 min to ensure the surface of Ni foam was cleaned. Both the Ni foam and the solution were transferred to a 50 ml Teflon-lined stainlesssteel autoclave. The as-prepared Ni foam was vertically immersed into the solution. The in-situ growth was carried out in an oven for 24 h at 180°C. After naturally cooling to room temperature, a thin brown film on the Ni foam was formed (NiFe-LDH). Subsequently, NiFe-LDH was rinsed with water and MeOH for 3 min with ultrasonication assistance, then dried at 80°C overnight. Powder form (NiFe-LDHp) collected by scraping.

nodes.name: Cl-Pt/LDH Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Three-electrode system: NiFe-LDH (1 cm² geometric area) as working electrode, graphite rod as counter electrode, Hg/HgO as reference electrode. NiFe-LDH firstly activated by CV (10 mV/s, 0.05 to -0.50 V vs RHE, 30 cycles) in 1 M KOH. Then transferred to 1 M KOH + 0.15 mmol/L H2PtCl6 for Pt electrodeposition by CV (5 mV/s, 0.05 to -0.50 V vs RHE, 40 cycles). Powder-based Cl-Pt/LDHp fabricated from NiFe-LDHp by CV (50 mV/s, 0.05 to -0.70 V vs RHE, 20 cycles).

nodes.name: HO-Pt/LDH Light Irradiation
nodes.procedure: The Cl ligand can be removed and replaced by the hydroxide group under the irradiation of visible light in water. PLS-SXE300 from Beijing perfectlight with a spectral region from 320 nm to 780 nm was used as the light source with an output power density of 3.75 mW cm−2. After 30 min irradiation, the HO-Pt/LDH was fabricated after the washing and drying process.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of HO-Pt/LDH ... After 30 min irradiation, the HO-Pt/LDH was fabricated after the washing and drying process.

nodes.name: R-X-Pt/LDH Impregnation
nodes.procedure: The axial-ligand on Pt-single-atom can be easily reversed from hydroxide group to halogen by simple impregnation strategy. In a typical process, the R-F-Pt/LDH was fabricated by immersed HO-Pt/LDH in 2 M NaF solution at 40°C for 4 h under magnetic stirring. Similarly, R-Cl-Pt/LDH, R-Br-Pt/LDH and R-I-Pt/LDH can be synthesized by changing the solution into NaCl, NaBr, and NaI, respectively.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of R-X-Pt/LDH (X = F, Cl, Br, or I) ... R-Cl-Pt/LDH, R-Br-Pt/LDH and R-I-Pt/LDH can be synthesized by changing the solution into NaCl, NaBr, and NaI, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cl-Pt/LDH and NiFe-LDH show nearly identical XRD patterns matching JCPDS No. 40-0215, indicating the crystalline structure of LDH remains unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared samples show nearly identical X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns as the NiFe-LDH support (Supplementary Fig. 1, JCPDS No. 40-0215), suggesting that the crystalline structure of the LDH remains.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both NiFe-LDH and Pt-loaded LDH exhibit plate-like nanosheet array with lateral size of ~500 nm and thickness of ~10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show that both the pristine NiFe-LDH and Pt-loaded LDH exhibit plate-like nanosheet array with lateral size of ∼500 nm and thickness of ∼10 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: No sub-nanometer clusters or nanoparticles detected; only discrete bright dots confirming atomic dispersion of Pt-atoms in Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No sub-nanometer clusters or nanoparticles were detected via aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM, Fig. 1c), except discrete bright dots, confirming the atomic dispersion of Pt-atoms in Cl-Pt/LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringe with interplanar spacing of 2.38 Å corresponds to (015) planes of NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the lattice fringe with interplanar spacing of about 2.38 Å corresponds to the (015) planes of NiFe-LDH, in line with the XRD results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distributions of Pt and O on Cl-Pt/LDH nanoplates confirm homogeneous dispersion of Pt-atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the uniform distributions of Pt and O on the nanoplates (Fig. 1d, g, and Supplementary Fig. 4) suggest that the Pt-atoms are homogeneously dispersed on the LDH substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Decreased signal at 329 cm^-1 after irradiation confirms loss of Pt-Cl bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the decreased signal at 329 cm^-1 in the Far-Infrared spectra after the irradiation further confirms the loss of the coulombic Pt-Cl bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Obvious changes in LMCT induced absorption bands (200-300 nm) between Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH while MMCT remains unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Obvious changes were also observed for the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) induced absorption bands (−200−300 nm) in Ultraviolet-visible Diffuse Reflectance spectra (UVvis DRS) of Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Profound radical signals appear for Cl-Pt/LDH under light, attributed to Cl radicals captured by DMPO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1j, profound radical signals were appeared when exposing the Cl-Pt/LDH to light and the radical scavenger 5,5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline N-oxide (DMPO) spontaneously.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt loadings in Cl-Pt/LDH, HO-Pt/LDH and R-X-Pt/LDH are very close.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Worth noting, the loadings of Pt in Cl-Pt/LDH, HO-Pt/LDH and R-X-Pt/LDH (X = F, Cl, Br, or I) are very close based on results of Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectrometer (ICP-AES) (Supplementary Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Loss of Cl 2p signal after irradiation; Pt 4f7/2 peaks between Pt^2+ (72.7 eV) and Pt^4+ (74.9 eV); slightly higher BE in Cl-Pt/LDH than HO-Pt/LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed to analyse the detailed chemical composition of Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH. The loss of Cl 2p signal (Fig. 2a) after light irradiation provides further evidence for the complete ligand exchange.

properties.intensity_profile: high intensity with peaks around 198-201 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: White lines of Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH locate between K2PtCl4 (Pt^2+) and PtO2 (Pt^4+); valence states estimated as 2.78 and 2.08 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2c, the white lines of both Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH locate between those of the K2PtCl4 (Pt2+) and PtO2 (Pt4+), suggesting that the valence states of Pt-atoms in Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH are between +2 and +4.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Pt-Pt at ~2.50 Å confirms atomic dispersion; Cl-Pt/LDH shows Pt-O at 1.60 Å and Pt-Cl at 2.06 Å; HO-Pt/LDH shows only Pt-O at ~1.60 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2d, no Pt-Pt interactions at ∼2.50 Å can be detected in both Cl-Pt/LDH and HO-Pt/LDH, demonstrating the atomic dispersion of Pt-atoms in these samples.
